h: Around Whitechapel and the city centre
p: Metquarter is a smart place to dip into on a busy day in town. Moorfields station is a short walk away, and Lime Street is also within walking distance, so it's easy to reach whether you're coming in by train or already exploring on foot.

Its size is a real plus. Unlike sprawling shopping centres, you can browse it without getting lost or worn out, which makes it a good choice if you just want a relaxed hour, a bite to eat and a bit of a nosy around. The food hall is the main draw for many, especially if you're in a group where everyone fancies something different.

Step outside and you're in the thick of it. Williamson Square, home to the Liverpool Playhouse theatre, is close by, and St John's Beacon, the tall tower with the viewing platform, rises above the city centre nearby. The Cavern Quarter, around Mathew Street, is a short walk away for Beatles history and live music, and the Cavern Club itself is one of the city's most famous music venues.

Fancy some more food after your browse? Bold Street, a short walk up the hill from the centre, is lined with independent restaurants and cafés. If it's culture you're after, St George's Hall and the World Museum near Lime Street are both striking places to visit.
It's handy as a mid-afternoon refuel stop too, between sightseeing and a show.
